optionReasons.saa-med-111:option:1: It's the closest because you use the right message. (SQS durable) — with UMA rows the two groups of workers COMPETEM by messages: each event is consumed by one process, not by both; independent delivery for both requires fan-out of SNS with one row per process.
optionReasons.saa-med-111:option:2: Polling in table of the DynamoDB reinvents row without its warranties — query latency, no visibility or redirect.
optionReasons.saa-med-111:option:3: Chaining processes by so-called syncrona creates the coupling that is to be avoided: transcription out of the air would stop the thumbnails.

finalJustifications: Because the fan-out SNS→SQS deliver an event COPY to each row: thumbnails and transcript process independently and sustainably — one out of the air does not affect the other.
Because the topic SNS holds events published by 14 days and each row reads them at its own pace, ensuring the independence of the processes.
Because SNS converts the event to the format of each worker before delivery, and it is this translation that isolates the two processes between themselves.
Because the two rows SQS share the same underlying buffer of the topic SNS, and the SNS coordinate which of the processes reads each message.

optionReasons.saa-med-112:option:0: It's the closest because a Lambda scheduled calling the snapshot APIs FUNCIONA — but it is a code of its own to maintain, without declaratory retention policies or conformity reports; AWS Backup delivers all this managed by tags.
optionReasons.saa-med-112:option:1: The DLM copper only EBS (and AMIs) — would leave RDS and EFS in the same decentralized mess as before.
optionReasons.saa-med-112:option:3: Version S3 protects objects from S3 — copy EBS/RDS/EFS 'for a bucket' is not a managed backup mechanism.

finalJustifications: Because AWS Central backup EBS, RDS and EFS a single plan: declarative scheduling and retention, ready-made labelling and compliance reports.
Because AWS Backup converts existing team snapshots into a unified format, consolidating legacy automatically.
Because AWS Backup replicates each backup to a secondary region by default, warranty required by compliance reports.
Because AWS Backup eliminates backup windows when using continuous replication, and compliance comes from the absence of snapshots.

optionReasons.saa-med-115:option:0: Reboot by CPU high treats software overload — does not detect or resolve host hardware failure.
optionReasons.saa-med-115:option:1: It's the closest because a ASG size 1 also recovers the application automatically — but launching an instance NOVA: other ID, other private IP, zero metadata; preserving identity requires the alarm 'recover' action in StatusCheckFailed_System.
optionReasons.saa-med-115:option:2: The Trusted Advisor recommend and notify — does not perform any recovery; e-mail to administrator is manual intervention.

finalJustifications: Because the alarm in StatusCheckFailed_System with 'recover' action migrates the instance to healthy hardware preserving ID, IPs, Elastic IP and metadata — without manual intervention.
Because the recovery action restores the last snapshot of the instance in another AZ, keeping the address through the Elastic IP reset.
Because the alarm triggers the support of AWS, which changes the faulty hardware of the host and reconnects the same instance in a few minutes.
Because the action recovers converts the instance into a AMI and automatically restarts, cloning metadata to the new generated ID.

optionReasons.saa-med-116:option:0: Larger instances remain the same point of failure — if the layer falls, static and dynamic fall together.
optionReasons.saa-med-116:option:1: It's the closest because caching the ready answers would even reduce the load — but ElastiCache is just behind the application layer: with the unavailable instances, no one is looking for the cache; resilience comes from serving the static on an independent path (S3 + CloudFront).
optionReasons.saa-med-116:option:3: Volumes EBS extras in the same instances keep the static hostage of the same fleet — nothing changes in failure.

finalJustifications: Because S3 + CloudFront creates a delivery path INDEPENDENTE of fleet EC2: the home page and the static remain in the air even with the degraded application layer.
Because CloudFront detects the layer drop EC2 and generates dynamic pages on the edge from the static of the S3.
Because S3 assumes the login requests when the application saturates, authenticating users by active session pocket.
Because CloudFront prioritizes the traffic of static content over the dynamic, reserving the capacity of the EC2 for the login.

optionReasons.saa-med-117:option:0: A unique sub-network in UMA AZ is the single point of failure by definition — the fall of the zone takes everything.
optionReasons.saa-med-117:option:2: Public sub-networks for banking and application expose internal layers to the internet — resilience does not justify opening the perimeter.
optionReasons.saa-med-117:option:3: It's the closest because it starts right — the multi-AZ web layer — but to half: application and bank in a single AZ continue to fall with it, taking down the entire site behind a ALB healthy; the requirement requires TODAS the layers in at least two AZs.

finalJustifications: Because the standard design is this: each layer with subnets in at least two AZs (public for web/ALB, private for app and bank) — the fall of an area does not drop any layer.
Because the mirrored subnets maintain synchronous replicas of each instance in the two AZs, and the failure is done by the router of the VPC.
Because the public sub-network absorbs private layer traffic when an AZ fails, functioning as a contingency route of VPC.
Because two AZs fold the CIDR available from VPC, and is the extra address space that ensures recovery of layers in failure.

optionReasons.saa-med-121:option:0: CRR for us-east-1 would take data from Brazilian territory — directly violates regulatory requirements.
optionReasons.saa-med-121:option:1: Version protects against overwritten in MESMA account — compromised credentials also delete versions; the requirement requires separate copy account.
optionReasons.saa-med-121:option:2: It's the closest because the AWS Backup cross-account is a real protection against compromise — but variant CROSS-REGION send copies out of Brazil; residence + separate account if resolved with SRR for another account in sa-east-1.

finalJustifications: Because the SRR replicates objects to a pocket of OUTRA counting keeping everything in sa-east-1: protection against exclusion and compromise without data leaving Brazil.
Because the SRR keeps the two accounts synchronized in both directions, and any accidental exclusion is undone by the mirror copy.
Because the SRR encrypts the replica with an exclusive key to the destination account, unreadable to the original compromised credentials.
Because the SRR freezes replica in mode only permanent reading, immune to any change from the account of origin.

optionReasons.saa-med-124:option:0: EventBridge without orchestrator publishes loose events — still without state, without configurable retry and without flow visibility.
optionReasons.saa-med-124:option:2: A unique giant function worsens: without resuming by step, the timeout of 15 minutes turn the roof of the entire flow.
optionReasons.saa-med-124:option:3: It's the closest because the direct chaining Lambda-for-Lambda in fact executes the flow — but distributes the orchestration by the code of each function: manual recesses, invisible state and no resume; Step Functions deliver this declarative, with Retry/Catch and history by execution.

finalJustifications: Because Step Functions defines the flow as a state machine: Retry and Declarative Catch by step, visible status of each execution and resumed without orchestration code.
Because Step Functions merges the four Lambdas into a single managed runtime, eliminating latency between the steps of the order.
Because Step Functions automatically reverses the completed steps when a failure, undoing the inconsistent order at the time.
Because Step Functions delegate the withdrawals to the internal row of each Lambda, and the state is recorded in the logs of CloudWatch.

optionReasons.saa-med-126:option:0: It is the closest because it would mount a real redundancy with right services — but weighted routing always divides traffic (not only in failure), duplicates distributions and depends on TTL of DNS; the native failover by status codes is the Origin Group in a distribution only.
optionReasons.saa-med-126:option:1: A CRR keeps the backup pocket synchronized — but no configuration in CloudFront, no one redirects the requests to him in failure.
optionReasons.saa-med-126:option:3: TTL longer only prolongs what is already in cache — miss cache during unavailability continues to fail.

finalJustifications: Because Origin Group defines primary and secondary in the same distribution: in configured error codes, the CloudFront resets the request in the backup pocket automatically.
Because Origin Group synchronizes the two bucks between them, dispensing the CRR and keeping backup identical to the main in real time.
Because Origin Group divides the requests between the two origins continuously, and healthy absorbs everything in the failure of the other origin.
Because Origin Group promotes the backup bucket the main one permanently to the first error HTTP detected at primary origin.
